About me

I’m building a new career in IT and cybersecurity in Auckland, bringing a background in electrical work, technical field service and small-business management.

My background

Originally from France, I’ve worked with customers in both France and New Zealand, finding faults, completing installations and explaining technical problems. My experience includes installing home automation and alarm systems from start to finish, from cabling through to configuration, testing and commissioning. Reading technical drawings and turning documentation into a working installation have been central to my work.

Since November 2025, I’ve been studying IT and cybersecurity full-time. I’ve earned CompTIA A+, Network+ and Security+ and am currently working towards the EC-Council CEH certification. I use guided training and a personal virtual lab to develop my understanding of systems, networking and security.

Why cybersecurity

I’ve always been curious about computing: what happens behind the screen, how systems communicate and how things can be adapted, repaired or protected. This career change is my opportunity to turn that curiosity into professional work.

My electrical background also sparked an interest in physical security. While working on sites in Auckland, I sometimes noticed how readily my presence as a contractor was accepted without much checking. It made me think about how physical access, trust and everyday habits affect security.

That connection between technology and people interests me. I’m particularly drawn to physical security, ethical security testing and helping people understand cybersecurity risks and protect themselves.

What I bring to a team

I’m used to working independently, investigating problems and taking responsibility for completed work. Working with customers and other trades has taught me to listen, explain findings clearly and coordinate practical solutions. Running a small business also gave me experience of balancing customer needs, costs and operational priorities.

I’m keen to contribute that experience to an IT support, networking or cybersecurity team in Auckland while learning from experienced colleagues. I’m interested in entry-level roles, whether full-time or part-time, as well as internships and job shadowing that would help me build professional experience.
